title: Unprotected Privileged Function
summary: A treasury guards withdrawAll() with an owner check, but leaves the setOwner() setter wide open. One unprotected privileged function undermines every other guard.
web2Analog: A broken access-control check (IDOR / missing authorization): an endpoint that lets any caller perform an admin-only action.

identify.question: Which function lets anyone take control of the treasury?
options: setOwner() — changes the owner with no access control
the constructor — sets the initial owner
identify.explanation: setOwner() has no access control, so any caller can make themselves the owner and then pass the withdrawAll() owner check. A privileged setter must be restricted (e.g. onlyOwner).

hints: withdrawAll() correctly requires you to be the owner — so how could an attacker satisfy that check?
Look at every state-changing function, not just the withdraw path. Which one changes who the owner is?
setOwner() has no msg.sender check at all. Call it first, then withdraw.
